summary: Lane chars fails round 2. Its one open item, lead:fighter-tris (major), is still partly done. The done criterion is a perf_1080 --prod match peak of 500k triangles or less. It is not met, and it cannot be met from files chars owns. The refix's claims re-measure true. The LOD1 recipe re-runs exactly. My own LOD1 match run, on the same build, reproduces the yield: peak 906,722 against the claimed 906,950. The renderer still draws each fighter's full body in the main pass, and the best case with the LOD1 everywhere is still 407k over budget. The crowd is 305-334k of the peak frame. What is left belongs to the engine stitch lead:fighter-lod-render plus a crowd cut. No regression found.

items.evidence: (1) Renderer unchanged. No src/render commit since 43196565. lod.ts:5-17 still says 'Fighters and structures keep their full meshes in the main pass'. There is no simplifyWithAttributes and no head lock in src/render. A correction to round 1: lodSwitch.outline defaults to false (lod.ts:96), but renderer.ts:472 sets it true in a match. So the fighters' rest-outline hull already uses lod.ts's generic 6 mm hull LOD (actors.ts:979 outlineGeometry). The body, flash and x-ray are still full. (2) Recipe re-run. `node art/blender/fighters/_lod1.mjs --json _harness/_reports/integ_chars_ver2_lod1.json`: 48 GLBs, 955,762 -> 580,849 (0.608), worst error 10 mm, 152,516 of 152,516 head-locked triangles kept, 0.82445-1.23797 m/unit, per mesh and uniform. extentM is exactly 2x unitM on every row, 1.65-2.48 m, a plausible fighter box. `node art/blender/fighters/_lod1_three.mjs --json _harness/_reports/integ_chars_ver2_lod1_three.json` (GLTFLoader.parse in Node): 955,762 -> 580,696, 152,513 of 152,513 kept, 0 mismatches. The per-mesh dequantization fix from round 1 is applied. (3) The LOD1 GLBs I regenerated with `_lod1.mjs --write` for the 10 match fighters are byte-identical (cmp) to the copies the refix served. Only the body index changes, e.g. burdam body v17879 t19808 -> t12655, accent untouched (_harness/_reports/integ_chars_ver2_cmp.mjs). (4) My own match run on the same prod build: `LOD1_DIR=<regenerated dir> node --import _harness/_reports/integ_chars_r1_route_lod1.mjs _harness/perf_1080.mjs --prod --match-only --no-build`. render_bench.html mtime was 01:21:39 before and after, served 10/10. Result: peak 906,722 at 1266.6 s, 23 s over 500k, 13 of 130 10-s windows over, 41 programs at 15.2 s, 0 programs after 1:00 (_harness/_reports/integ_chars_ver2_match_lod1.json/.log). My peak-profile frame (1266.6 s) has the same crowd and structures as the refix's base run A at 1266.7 s: crowd 304,607, structures 79,519. That makes it a like-for-like fighter comparison. Fighters go 346,453 -> 233,366 (-113,087, -32.6 %); main 310,020 -> 198,257. The refix's A/B numbers check out: 1,045,468 -> 906,950 and 23 -> 12 windows, recomputed from both timelines. Late windows (>= 900 s): median -46.8k; the p10/p90 labels in integ_chars_r1_lod1_ab.txt are swapped, a cosmetic slip. (5) The low preset passes at 333,719 (integ_engine_v1_perf_1080.json). No shipped GLB changed: `git diff 43196565 HEAD --stat -- art/out/fighters` is empty. (6) The done criterion is still missed. Even with the LOD1 drawn everywhere, the match peak is 906,722 > 500,000. The program count is 41 > 40, but it is an early count at 14-15 s, not a late program. The chars lane is right that the rest is engine work.
items.fixHint: Engine stitch lead:fighter-lod-render. In a match, swap each fighter body's index for faceLockedLodIndex (art/blender/fighters/_lod1_three.mjs:52) after template.updateMatrixWorld(true) and before any pose, with lod.ts's MeshoptSimplifier after lodReady. Copy the function into src/render: the .mjs file imports gltf-transform, node:fs and _lod1.mjs at its top level, so src cannot import it as is. Then cut the crowd: 305-334k at the peak frame, and even with no crowd the LOD1 peak would be about 573-600k, so another group must also drop about 100k (vfx, canopy or structures). Bring programs to 40 or fewer in the first 15 s. Re-run perf_1080 --prod (low + match).
